quote: Frage A: Giebt es $C_6$ mit 11 getrennten Ovalen kann ich bisher nicht [-&-] beantworten.
english: Question A: Is there a $C_6$ with 11 separate ovals? I cannot answer this so far.
topic: Hilbert argues that for any mathematical question one can first ask whether it is decidable by finitely many operations, illustrates this with the existence of sextic curves with 11 separate ovals, and notes that not every integrity domain is finitely generated.

triage.modern_statement: Is there a smooth real plane projective algebraic curve of degree 6 (a sextic) with 11 ovals, the most allowed by Harnack's bound, where all 11 ovals are mutually exterior, i.e. unnested, each lying outside the others? This is the founding question of the first part of Hilbert's 16th problem: classifying how the ovals of a real algebraic curve can be arranged. (Harnack (1876) had already shown that sextics with 11 ovals exist, so here 'getrennt' most likely means 'unnested'.)
triage.answered_by: The answer is no. Hilbert claimed this was impossible (1891), and the question went into his 16th problem (1900). Petrovskii gave the first rigorous general proof (1933/38): his inequality gives an upper bound of 10 for sextics, which rules out 11 unnested ovals. Gudkov proved Hilbert's claim about 11-oval sextics in his 1954 Candidate (PhD) thesis. In 1969 he completed the full classification of how the ovals of a sextic can be arranged, finding a third arrangement for 11-oval sextics that Hilbert had believed impossible.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's problem began with the question of whether a degree-6 curve with 11 ovals (the maximum allowed by Harnack's bound) can have all its ovals disjoint. Petrovsky answered it negatively.

For sextics, Petrovskii's upper bound (1933/38) is 10, so a curve with 11 unnested ovals is ruled out. The source calls this hypothetical curve the 'Hilbert sextic' and cites Hilbert's 1891 statement that such a sextic cannot have all its ovals unnested.
In his 1954 Candidate dissertation, Gudkov proved Hilbert's statement about the topology of sextics with 11 components. His Doctor's thesis (1969) disproved part of it and gave the final answer.

Classifying 11-component sextics up to isotopy is a central part of Hilbert's 16th problem. Hilbert conjectured there were only two types. Gudkov disproved this in 1969 by constructing a third type, completing the degree-6 case.

triage.why: This note is the seed of Hilbert's 16th problem, first part. The question of whether a sextic can have 11 separate (unnested) ovals was settled negatively by Petrovskii's inequality (1933/38). Gudkov proved Hilbert's broader claim about 11-oval sextics in 1954, and in 1969 completed the classification of sextic oval arrangements, adding a third 11-oval type Hilbert thought impossible. Degree 6 is therefore closed. The wider 16th problem is still being researched, for example the isotopy classification for higher degrees. One caveat: I read 'getrennt' as 'mutually exterior/unnested'. If Hilbert meant only '11 ovals' in general, Harnack had already answered that in 1876.
